newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope cheerful after good night's rest.
newsitem.headline: Pope cheerful after good night's rest.

text.p: Pope John Paul was in a buoyant mood on Saturday and doctors said he was making a swift recovery four days after surgery to remove his appendix.
"All is proceeding in the best possible way and the Pope is in a fine mood," said Professor Luigi Ortona after visiting the Pope at Rome's Gemelli hospital.
"The Pope continues to get up and walk around and he has already begun to work with his aides," Ortona told reporters, adding that the 76-year-old Pontiff had slept well and showed no signs of fever.

The Polish-born Pope had a 50-minute operation at the Gemelli on Tuesday to remove an inflamed appendix. Doctors said biopsies showed that there was no trace of any recurrence of a colon tumour removed in 1992.
Vatican officials have said the Pope plans to celebrate his first public mass at the Vatican to mark a religious anniversary on October 27 but would probably resume short audiences earlier.

The Pope, who marks the 18th anniversary of his 1978 election next Wednesday, is keen to be in good form by November 1, the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest. He has invited all priests ordained in 1946 to Rome to celebrate.
